abstract.para: Real-time applications require a hardware foundation configured for minimal latency. This section describes how to configure server BIOS and firmware settings. These adjustments eliminate low-level platform interference before you begin latency testing.

topic.para: Before you start measuring hardware or operating system latencies, you must optimize your machine settings:

step.para: Access your server BIOS or firmware settings.
Disable power-management features that introduce variable latency, since these are common sources of SMIs and scheduling jitter. Menu labels vary by vendor, but look for and disable:

listitem.para: P-states and frequency scaling (SpeedStep, Cool'n'Quiet or similar)
Any other SMI-generating power management feature

step.para: Reduce memory patrol scrubbing to its lowest available rate or disable it, since scrubbing cycles can introduce firmware-level latency spikes.
